scenes.headline: He had kept the light for forty years
scenes.narration: Every night for forty years, Tomas climbed the same ninety steps to light the lamp.

scenes.headline: That winter, the lamp was automated
scenes.narration: In his last winter a machine arrived. It could switch the light on and off, and it never needed a single step.

scenes.headline: He still climbed the stairs
scenes.narration: Each evening he climbed anyway, just to stand beside the light and watch the water turn dark.

media.query: lighthouse at dusk over dark water

scenes.headline: One night, the machine failed
scenes.narration: In a February storm the machine failed. The lamp went dark, and a fishing boat was somewhere out in the fog.

scenes.headline: Ninety steps, one match
scenes.narration: Tomas climbed faster than he had in years, and lit the old lamp by hand. The boat found the harbour by dawn.

scenes.headline: Some work still needs a person
scenes.narration: Technology helps, but someone still has to care enough to climb the stairs. Follow for more short stories.
